questions.text: According to the passage, what was detected in an environmental sample collected in Kolkata in April 2022?
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is Option 3.
 
Key Points
  • In April 2022, a case of vaccine-derived poliovirus was detected from an environmental sample collected in Kolkata.
  • After genetic sequencing, it was considered likely to be immunodeficiency-related vaccine-derived poliovirus (iVDPV).
  • The passage explicitly mentions vaccine-derived poliovirus, not the wild type.
Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.
 
Correct Information: "In April 2022, a case of vaccine-derived poliovirus was detected from an environmental sample collected in Kolkata."
 
Additional Information
  • 1) Wild poliovirus type 1 – Incorrect: The passage does not suggest that wild poliovirus type 1 was detected in Kolkata.
  • 2) Wild poliovirus type 2 – Incorrect: The passage does not indicate the detection of wild poliovirus type 2 in Kolkata.
  • 4) Circulating vaccinia virus – Incorrect: The passage does not mention vaccinia virus.
  • 5) Immunodeficiency-related vaccine-derived poliovirus (iVDPV) – Partially Correct: Although it was likely considered to be iVDPV, the detected virus is broadly referred to as vaccine-derived poliovirus in the passage.

questions.text: Which of the following statements is true according to the passage?

options.text: The child from Tikrikilla was conclusively diagnosed with wild poliovirus.
The switch from trivalent to bivalent oral polio vaccine in India occurred in 2015.
WPV type 2 was globally eradicated in 2016.
The last WPV type 3 case was reported globally in 2019.
Pakistan has reported zero WPV type 1 cases in 2024.

questions.explanation:
The correct answer is Option 4.
 
Key Points
  • Statement 1: The child from Tikrikilla was conclusively diagnosed with wild poliovirus.
    • This statement is incorrect as the passage states there is no official report confirming whether it is caused by wild poliovirus or vaccine-derived poliovirus.
  • Statement 2: The switch from trivalent to bivalent oral polio vaccine in India occurred in 2015.
    • This statement is incorrect as the passage mentions that the switch happened in 2016, not 2015.
  • Statement 3: WPV type 2 was globally eradicated in 2016.
    • This statement is incorrect as the passage states that WPV type 2 was eradicated in 2015.
  • Statement 4: The last WPV type 3 case was reported globally in 2019.
    • This statement is correct as the passage confirms, "the global eradication of the wild poliovirus (WPV) type 2 in 2015 and the WPV type 3 in 2019."
  • Statement 5: Pakistan has reported zero WPV type 1 cases in 2024.
    • This statement is incorrect as the passage mentions, "as of August 13, Afghanistan and Pakistan have reported 14 WPV type 1 cases this year."
Therefore, the correct answer is: ‘Option 4’.

questions.text: According to the passage, which of the following statements about the oral polio vaccine (OPV) in India is false?

options.text: India switched from trivalent to bivalent OPV in 2016.
Bivalent OPV contains live, attenuated type 1 and type 3 viruses.
Type 2 virus is included in the bivalent OPV given in India.
Immunodeficient children should not receive OPV.
The switch to IPV has been recommended but not executed in India.

questions.explanation:
The correct answer is Option 3.
 
Key Points
  • India switched from trivalent to bivalent oral polio vaccine (OPV) in 2016.
  • The bivalent OPV contains live, attenuated type 1 and type 3 viruses, not type 2 virus.
  • The passage mentions that it's impossible for the child to have the type 2 virus from the oral vaccine given in India because India made the switch to the bivalent vaccine, which does not include type 2 virus.
Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.
 
Correct Information: "India made the globally significant switch in 2016 from trivalent to bivalent oral polio vaccine that has only live, attenuated type 1 and type 3 virus."
 
Additional Information
  • Option 1) India switched from trivalent to bivalent OPV in 2016 – True: The passage confirms this switch.
  • Option 2) Bivalent OPV contains live, attenuated type 1 and type 3 viruses – True: The bivalent OPV includes these specific types.
  • Option 4) Immunodeficient children should not receive OPV – True: The passage explicitly mentions this recommendation.
  • Option 5) The switch to IPV has been recommended but not executed in India – True: The passage suggests an urgent need for the switch to IPV, which has not been fully implemented.

questions.text:
Based on the passage, which of the following sentences can be inferred about the urgency of switching to IPV in India?

A) Continuing to use OPV may result in future vaccine-derived poliovirus cases.

B) IPV would entirely eliminate the risk of poliovirus transmission.

C) India's healthcare system struggles to identify immunodeficient children.
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is 'Option 3'.
 
Key Points
  • A) Continuing to use OPV may result in future vaccine-derived poliovirus cases.
    • This can be inferred from the passage. The passage suggests that as long as OPV is used, there could be future vaccine-derived poliovirus cases, especially in immunodeficient individuals.
  • B) IPV would entirely eliminate the risk of poliovirus transmission.
    • This cannot be inferred from the passage. The passage advocates for the switch to IPV but does not state that it would entirely eliminate the risk of poliovirus transmission.
  • C) India's healthcare system struggles to identify immunodeficient children.
    • This can be inferred from the passage. The passage highlights the challenge in India’s healthcare system in identifying immunodeficient children before administering OPV.
Therefore, the correct answer is A and C.
 
Additional Information
  • Only A: Incorrect because both A and C can be inferred from the passage.
  • Only B: Incorrect because B cannot be inferred from the passage.
  • All A, B, and C: Incorrect because B cannot be inferred from the passage.
  • Only C: Incorrect because both A and C can be inferred from the passage.

questions.text: Which of the following words is similar in meaning to "intriguing" in the context of the passage?
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is: Option 2.

Key Points

  • The word "intriguing" means arousing one's curiosity or interest; fascinating. (दिलचस्प)
    • Example: The scientist shared some intriguing discoveries about space.
  • "Puzzling" refers to something that causes confusion or is difficult to understand. (पेचीदा/उलझन भरा)
    • Example: The sudden disappearance of the keys was puzzling to everyone.

Therefore, the correct answer is: puzzling.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • Uninteresting (रुचिहीन): Not arousing interest; dull.
    • Example: The lecture was uninteresting and many students fell asleep.
  • Obvious (स्पष्ट): Easily perceived or understood; clear and apparent.
    • Example: It was obvious that he was not interested in the conversation.
  • Predictable (पूर्वानुमेय): Expected; able to be foreseen or anticipated.
    • Example: The outcome of the game was predictable from the start.
  • Minor (छोटा): Lesser in importance, seriousness, or significance.
    • Example: The accident caused only minor damage to the car.

questions.text:
Given Below is a sentence with two blanks. Identify the correct order of words which can be used to fill in the blanks.

The menu at Sam’s Riverside is _______ by seasonality, so very little is now _______ in Europe.

A. Dictated
B. Portrait 
C. Spurned
D. Refused
E. Sourced
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is AE.

Key Points

  • Let us see the meanings of the given words:
    • Dictated - controlled or decisively affected; determined.
    • Portrait - denoting a format of printed matter which is higher than it is wide.
    • Spurned - rejected with disdain or contempt.
    • Refused - indicated or showed that one is not willing to do something.
    • Sourced - found out where (something) can be obtained.

Important Points

  • In the sentence, the menu at Sam's depends on seasons—items will only be available for a certain season. So, 'Dictated' is the correct word for the first blank. 
  • Since the menu is seasonal we get the hint that they are not getting much from Europe because of the current season. So, 'Sourced' must be the correct word for the second blank. 
  • From the meanings given, the words 'Dictated' and 'Sourced' are grammatically and conceptually correct.​​


So the correct sentence is - The menu at Sam’s Riverside is dictated by seasonality, so very little is now sourced in Europe.

questions.text:
Given below is a sentence with two blanks. Identify the correct order of words which can be used to fill in the blanks.

The environment and urban planning minister, Murat Kurum said people were ________ under the wreckage and rescue efforts were ________. 

A. Contradict
B. Underway
C. Refute
D. Trapped
E. Hefty
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is DB.

Key Points

  • Let us see the meanings of the given words:
    • Contradict - deny the truth of (a statement) by asserting the opposite.
    • Underway - having started and in progress; being done or carried out.
    • Refute - prove (a statement or theory) to be wrong or false; disprove.
    • Trapped - unable to move or escape as a result of obstruction.
    • Hefty - large and heavy.

Important Points

  • From words like 'wreckage' and 'rescue efforts' we can understand that people were caught in the wreckage and unable to move. So, 'Trapped' is the correct word for the first blank. 
  • We can understand from the given sentence that rescue efforts were in progress. So, 'Underway' is the correct word for the second blank. 
  • From the meanings given, the words 'Trapped' and 'Underway' are grammatically and conceptually correct.​​


So the correct sentence is - The environment and urban planning minister, Murat Kurum said people were trapped under the wreckage and rescue efforts were underway.

questions.text:
Select the phrase/connector from the given three options which can be used to form a single sentence from the two sentences given below, implying the same as expressed in the statement sentences.

Sharma was a contemporary of such political stalwarts as Arun Jaitley, Abhishek Singhvi and Vijay Goel. He was a rising political star when he cut his own career short by killing his wife in 1995.

1. After being a contemporary of

2. Being a contemporary of such political

3. Since he was a rising political star
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is Only 2.
Key Points

  • The phrase that can connect both the given sentences and imply the same meaning is only 2.
    • 'Being' is used with a person or thing that exists. The two statements talk about "Sharma". The first states whose contemporary he was, while the second states how he cut his political career by killing his wife. Clearly, the above synthesis is both grammatically and contextually correct.
  • 'After being a contemporary': at a later or future time; afterwards. The second statement is not a consequence of the first one. Hence, this option is ruled out.
  • ​'Since': from a particular time in the past until a later time, or until now. The two statements do not show a cause and effect relationship, thus, since, can be eliminated.


The sentence after using the phrase is-

  • Being a contemporary of such political stalwarts as Arun Jaitley, Abhishek Singhvi and Vijay Goel, Sharma, was a rising political star who cut his own career short by killing his wife in 1995.

Additional Information

Let us understand the meanings of some important words:

  • Contemporary: belonging to the same or a stated period in the past
  • Stalwarts: a loyal, reliable, and hard-working supporter of or participant in an organization

questions.text:
Select the phrase/connector from the given three options which can be used to form a single sentence from the two sentences given below, implying the same as expressed in the statement sentences.

N95 is not required and people can stay comfortable and protected. This is possible only when everyone is wearing a mask.

1. If people can stay comfortable 

2. If everyone is wearing a mask

3. If N95 is not required
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is option 2 i.e. only 2.

 Explanation      

  • The phrase that can connect both the given sentences and imply the same meaning is the second one.
    • 'If' is used to say that one thing can, will or might happen or be true, depending on another thing happening or being true.

The sentence after using the phrase is- If everyone is wearing a mask, N95 is not required and people can stay comfortable and protected.

  • The sentence means that N95 is not required and people can stay comfortable and protected only when everyone is wearing a mask i.e. one thing is true only when the other thing connected to it is true.​

questions.text:
Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error.

Every student in the  (a) / class contribute actively during (b)  / discussions, fostering a collaborative learning environment. (c) / More than one of the above (d) / None of the above (e)
questions.explanation:
The erroneous part is 'b'.

Key Points

  • The error in the sentence is in Part: "class contribute actively during."
  • The correct form should be "contributes actively during" instead of "contribute actively during."
  • The subject-verb agreement is incorrect in this sentence. When using "every," it indicates singular and requires a singular verb form to match.
  • In this case, "Every student" is the subject, and "student" is singular. Therefore, the verb should also be singular to agree with the subject.
  • Example: 
    • Correct: Every student in the class contributes actively during discussions.
    • Incorrect: Every student in the class contribute actively during discussions.
  • The corrected sentence maintains proper subject-verb agreement by using the singular verb "contributes" to match the singular subject "Every student." 
     

Correct Sentence: Every student in the class contributes actively during discussions, fostering a collaborative learning environment.

questions.text:
Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error.

The book, along with  (a) / its accompanying illustrations (b) /, provide a comprehensive understanding of the historical era. (c) / More than one of the above (d) / None of the above (e)
questions.explanation:
The erroneous part is 'c'.

Key Points

  • The error in the sentence is in Part]: "provide a comprehensive understanding of the historical era."
  • The correct form should be "provides a comprehensive" instead of "provide a comprehensive."
  • When a sentence includes a subject along with a phrase such as "along with," "as well as," or "together with," the subject-verb agreement is determined by the main subject before the phrase, not by the words within the phrase.
  • In this case, "The book" is the main subject, and "its accompanying illustrations" is a phrase providing additional information. The main subject, "The book," is singular, so the verb "provides" should also be singular to agree with the subject.
  • Example:
    • Singular Subject: The book, along with its author, provides insight into historical events.
    • Incorrect Plural Verb: The book, along with its author, provide insight into historical events.
  • The corrected sentence would read: "The book, along with its accompanying illustrations, provides a comprehensive understanding of the historical era."
  • This adjustment ensures proper subject-verb agreement, where the singular subject requires a singular verb.

questions.text:
Direction: Evaluate the following word, accompanied by three sentences containing it. Determine the sentence(s) that accurately convey the meaning of the given word.
 
Prodigiously
 
A. Carlos Alcaraz is a prodigiously talented player who has already won multiple Grand Slam titles.
B. Prodigiously nervous, the pianist played with a trembling hand throughout the concert.
C. The prodigiously massive library contains volumes from ancient to modern times.
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is: Option 2 - Both A & C.

Key Points

  • The word "Prodigiously" means to an unusually great, remarkable, or impressive degree; enormously. (असाधारण रूप से, बहुत अधिक)
    • Example: The young athlete has improved prodigiously over the past year.
  • "Prodigiously talented" means exceptionally or extraordinarily talented, making sentence A an appropriate use of the word. (असाधारण रूप से प्रतिभाशाली)
    • Example: Carlos Alcaraz is a prodigiously talented player who has achieved remarkable success at a young age.
  • "Prodigiously massive" means extremely or extraordinarily large, making sentence C an appropriate use of the word. (असाधारण रूप से विशाल)
    • Example: The museum houses a prodigiously massive collection of historical manuscripts.
  • Sentence B is not an appropriate use of "prodigiously" because the word is generally used to emphasize an unusually great degree of size, quantity, ability, or achievement rather than a temporary emotional state such as nervousness.

Therefore, the correct answer is- Both A & C.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and examples:

  • Only A (केवल A): This option is incorrect because sentence C also uses "prodigiously" appropriately.
    • Example: Sentence A correctly describes an exceptionally talented player.
  • Only C (केवल C): This option is incorrect because sentence A also correctly conveys the meaning of "prodigiously."
    • Example: The scientist was prodigiously successful in his research.
  • All A, B & C (A, B और C सभी): This option is incorrect because sentence B uses "prodigiously nervous" in an unsuitable context.
    • Example: The phrase "prodigiously nervous" does not appropriately convey the intended meaning of the word.
  • None of these (इनमें से कोई नहीं): This option is incorrect because sentences A and C correctly use the word "prodigiously."
    • Example: The artist was prodigiously talented and produced an extraordinary body of work.

questions.text:
Directions: Evaluate the following word, accompanied by three sentences containing it. Determine the sentence(s) that accurately convey the meaning of the given word.
Condone

A. The principal could not condone such rude behaviour in the school.

B. We cannot condone any form of discrimination in our company.

C. She condone the delicious food at the new restaurant.
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is option 2.

Key Points

  • To answer this question, let's first understand the meaning of the word given in the question:
  • Condone: to accept or allow behaviour that is morally wrong or offensive to continue. (अनदेखी करना, माफ़ करना)
  • Now, let's examine the given sentences:
  • Sentence A: The principal could not condone such rude behaviour in the school.
    • This sentence correctly uses the word "condone" to describe the principal not accepting rude behavior.
  • Sentence B: We cannot condone any form of discrimination in our company.
    • This sentence also correctly uses the word "condone" to describe not accepting any form of discrimination.
  • Sentence C: She condone the delicious food at the new restaurant.
    • This sentence incorrectly uses the word "condone," as it does not fit the context of accepting or allowing morally wrong behavior.
  • So, both sentences A and B correctly use the word "condone" to illustrate not accepting certain behaviors, while sentence C does not.

Therefore, the correct answer is "Both A & B."

questions.text:
Direction: Evaluate the following word, accompanied by three sentences containing it. Determine the sentence(s) that accurately convey the meaning of the given word.
 
Perpetuate
 
A. The government’s ineffective policies could perpetuate poverty in the region.
B. They sought to perpetuate the charitable traditions started by their ancestors.
C. The artist wanted to perpetuate his ideas into the canvas quickly.
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is option 2.

Key Points

  • To answer this question, let's first understand the meaning of the word given in the question:
  • Perpetuate: to cause (something that should be stopped, such as a mistaken idea or a bad situation) to continue. (स्थायी बनाना, बनाए रखना)
  • Now, let's examine the given sentences:
  • Sentence A: The government’s ineffective policies could perpetuate poverty in the region.
    • This sentence correctly uses the word "perpetuate" to describe the continuation of poverty due to ineffective policies.
  • Sentence B: They sought to perpetuate the charitable traditions started by their ancestors.
    • This sentence also correctly uses the word "perpetuate" to describe the continuation of charitable traditions.
  • Sentence C: The artist wanted to perpetuate his ideas into the canvas quickly.
    • This sentence does not correctly use the word "perpetuate" as it implies causing something to continue, not the act of transferring ideas quickly.
  • So, both sentences A and B correctly use the word "perpetuate" to illustrate different contexts of causing something to continue.

Therefore, the correct answer is "Both A & B."

questions.text:
Direction: In the following question, a sentence is given divided into four parts (A), (B), (C) and (D). The error, if any, will only be in one part of the sentence. Choose the option with the part containing the error and mark it as your answer. If the sentence is free from errors, mark 'No error' as your answer.

The Japanese investment powerhouse (A)/ SoftBank would injects capital into (B)/ WeWork and take a controlling stake, a (C)/ move the company's management hopes to avoid (D).
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is Option 1.

Key Points 

  • Part (B) of the sentence i.e. "SoftBank would injects capital into" is erroneous.
    • The modal verb 'would' always takes verb in the base form of the verb.
      • Example: He would come today.
    • 'Injects' is not the base form of verb.
    • Base form is "Inject."
    • Hence, option 1 is the correct answer.
  • The correct answer would be: "The Japanese investment powerhouse SoftBank would inject capital into WeWork and take a controlling stake, a move the company's management hopes to avoid."
    ​

Additional Information 

  • Modal verbs are verbs like should, can, could, might, will etc.
  • 'Be' and 'have' are not modal verbs.
  • They are normal verbs but can also be used as auxiliary verbs to form questions and other forms.

questions.explanation:
The correct answer is Option 4.

Key Points

Seeming emerging from nothing, India's IT-service (A)/ industry became a giant in just 20 years, generating (B)/ more than 70% of its revenues through exports to developed (C)/ markets and creating jobs in the process (D).
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is Option 2.

Key Points

  • Part (A) of the sentence i.e. "Seeming emerging from nothing​" is erroneous.

    • The adverb 'seemingly' should be used here instead.

Additional Information

  • It also has the property of describing the adjective or another adverb.
  • Unlike other parts of speech, adverbs can be placed at any part of the sentence (beginning, middle or end), and make complete sense without sounding absurd.

  • "Developed markets" means The markets that are big and have a lot of business opportunities.

questions.text: Which of the following words cannot fill the blank that is labeled (A)?
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is 'ignorance'.

Key Points 

  • The sentence which contains the blank is "A day of _____(A)_____of the Pulwama attack passed yet again last month.​"
  • The given sentence states that the day of recognition of the Pulwama attack passed yet again last month. 
  • Hence, as per the context of the given sentence the most suitable words will be- recollection, reminiscence, remembrance, anamnesis, etc.
  • All the above-mentioned words are synonyms of each other.
  • The word 'ignorance' means lack of knowledge or information. (ज्ञान या जानकारी का अभाव।)
    • Usage:- "he acted in ignorance of basic procedures"​
      • Hence, 'ignorance' will be not suitable for the blank as per the context of the given sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 5.

Additional Information

Hence, CP for Mayank = Rs.70400

So, the SP for Mayank = [(100 + 20)/100] × 70400 = Rs.84480

∴ The price at which Mayank should sell the car to Bharat is Rs.84480

questions.text: Which of the following options states the correct storage device hierarchy in terms of decreasing access time?

options.text: magnetic tape, magnetic disk, cache, main memory
magnetic disk, optical disk, main memory, register
magnetic tape, magnetic disk, main memory, register
main memory, register, magnetic disk, magnetic tape
register, main memory, magnetic disk, magnetic tape

questions.explanation:
The correct answer is register, main memory, magnetic disk, magnetic tape 

Key Points

  • The hierarchy of storage devices in terms of decreasing access time. Answer covered: register, main memory, magnetic disk, magnetic tape 

Additional Information

  • Registers: These are the smallest and fastest type of memory in a computer. They sit within the CPU (Central Processing Unit) itself and are used for storing the immediate data that the CPU needs to perform computations. The number of registers, which can vary depending on the CPU's architecture, is limited because they are expensive and consume more power.
  • Cache memory (or CPU Cache): This is a very fast and small amount of memory that is built directly into the CPU or located next to it. It is used to store frequently used data to decrease the time needed to access this data. The cache memory is faster to access than RAM. There are usually multiple levels of cache (L1, L2, L3, etc.), with L1 being the fastest and smallest, and each subsequent level being larger and moderately slower.
  • Main memory (RAM - Random Access Memory): Main memory is a type of computer memory that can be read and changed in any order, typically used to store working data and machine code. It is much larger than the cache but slower to access. RAM is volatile, which means it loses its content once power is turned off.
  • Secondary memory (Hard Disk, Solid State Drives): Also known as storage, it is non-volatile, meaning it retains its contents even when the computer is turned off. Magnetic Hard Disk Drives (HDD) and Solid State Drives (SSD) are the most common examples. SSDs are faster but more expensive than HDDs.
  • Optical Disks: Storage devices which use lasers to read/write data, such as CDs, DVDs, and Blu-Ray discs. They usually have less storage capacity and slower access times than hard drives but are useful for distributing software, music, and movies due to their portability.
  • Magnetic Tape: These are used primarily for data backup and archiving. They can store larges amounts of data affordably but have very slow access times because they are a sequential access data storage device, meaning data must be read in the order it was originally written which is slower than the direct access provided by disks.

All these types of memory and storage form part of a system's memory hierarchy, which manages access speed, cost, size, and volatility.

questions.text: In which of the following states the transaction executes all its operations successfully and all the effects are now permanently saved on the database system?
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is Committed

  • Active state: The active state is the first state of every transaction. In this state, the transaction is being executed.
  • Partially committed: In the partially committed state, a transaction executes its final operation, but the data is still not saved to the database.
  • Committed: A transaction is said to be in a committed state if it executes all its operations successfully. In this state, all the effects are now permanently saved on the database system.
  • Failed state: If any of the checks made by the database recovery system fails, then the transaction is said to be in the failed state.
  • Aborted: If any of the checks fail and the transaction has reached a failed state then the database recovery system will make sure that the database is in its previous consistent state. If not, then it will abort or roll back the transaction to bring the database into a consistent state.
  • If the transaction fails in the middle of the transaction then before executing the transaction, all the executed transactions are rolled back to its consistent state. After aborting the transaction, the database recovery module will select one of the two operations:
    • Re-start the transaction
    • Kill the transaction

questions.explanation:
A switch statement allows a variable to be tested for equality against a list of values. Each value is called a case, and the variable being switched on is checked for each switch case.

Syntax

switch(expression) {

case constant-expression :

statement(s);       break; /* optional */            

default : /* Optional */

statement(s);

}

Important Points :

  • The expression used in a switch statement must have an integral or enumerated type, or be of a class type in which the class has a single conversion function to an integral or enumerated type.
  • The constant-expression for a case must be the same data type as the variable in the switch, and it must be a constant or a literal.
  • When the variable being switched on is equal to a case, the statements following that case will execute until a break statement is reached.
  • When a break statement is reached, the switch terminates, and the flow of control jumps to the next line following the switch statement.
  • Not every case needs to contain a break. If no break appears, the flow of control will fall through to subsequent cases until a break is reached.
  • A switch statement can have an optional default case, which must appear at the end of the switch. The default case can be used for performing a task when none of the cases is true. No break is needed in the default case.

questions.text: Which of the following is an example of utility software?
questions.explanation: Text editors can be used to enter program language source statements or to create documents such as technical manuals. At its simplest, a backup utility might be a program within an OS designed to back up a laptop to an external drive. Enterprise backup utilities include programs designed to centrally back up applications such as databases or enterprise resource planning systems. A file compression utility is a software program that is used to compress or decompress files.
